retained_source_material_already_read.excerpt: The matrix solutions of an irreducible algebraic equation with integral coefficients were studied by Latimer and MacDuffee.

original_publisher_deposited_abstracts.text: <jats:p>The matrix solutions of an irreducible algebraic equation with integral coefficients were studied by Latimer and MacDuffee. They considered matrices with rational integers as elements. If A is such a matrix, then all matrices of the “class” S<jats:sup>1</jats:sup> A<jats:italic>S</jats:italic> will again be solutions if S is a matrix of determinant ± 1. On the other hand, in general all solutions cannot be derived in this way from one solution only. It was in fact shown that the number of classes of matrix solutions coincides with the number of different classes of ideals in the ring generated by an algebraic root of the same equation.</jats:p>

retained_source_material_already_read.excerpt: The main result proved in this paper is that the conjugacy problem in word-hyperbolic groups is solvable in linear time.

original_publisher_deposited_abstracts.text: <jats:p> The main result proved in this paper is that the conjugacy problem in word-hyperbolic groups is solvable in linear time. This is using a standard RAM model of computation, in which basic arithmetical operations on integers are assumed to take place in constant time. The constants involved in the linear time solution are all computable explicitly. </jats:p><jats:p> We also give a proof of the result of Mike Shapiro that in a word-hyperbolic group a word in the generators can be transformed into short-lex normal form in linear time. This is used in the proof of our main theorem, but is a significant theoretical result of independent interest, which deserves to be in the literature. Previously the best known result was a quadratic estimate. </jats:p>

retained_source_material_already_read.excerpt: An (non-practical) algorithm is described that, given as input two lists A and B

original_publisher_deposited_abstracts.text: <jats:p> Let G be a word-hyperbolic group with given finite generating set, for which various standard structures and constants have been pre-computed. An (non-practical) algorithm is described that, given as input two lists A and B, each composed of m words in the generators and their inverses, determines whether or not the lists are conjugate in G, and returns a conjugating element, should one exist. The algorithm runs in time O(mμ), where μ is an upper bound on the length of elements in the two lists. Similarly, an algorithm is outlined that computes generators of the centralizer of A, with the same bound on running time. </jats:p>
